question: In relation to clopidogrel, it is false that:

options.opa: It is structurally related to thienopyridines.
options.opb: It inhibits adenyl cyclase, and therefore increases cAMP levels.
options.opc: It has a low index of myelotoxicity in relation to ticlopidine.
options.opd: It has a longer action in relation to ticlopidine.
options.ope: In case of surgical intervention, it is recommended to interrupt the treatment at least one week in advance.

enhanced_information: Clopidogrel is indeed a thienopyridine derivative, confirming option (a) as true. Clopidogrel has a lower incidence of myelotoxicity compared to ticlopidine, making option (c) true. Clopidogrel has a shorter duration of action than ticlopidine, thus option (d) is false. Lastly, it is recommended to interrupt clopidogrel treatment at least one week prior to surgical intervention, confirming option (e) as true. Therefore, the false statements are (b) and (d).
analysis: Clopidogrel is a thienopyridine derivative, confirming option (a) as true. It works by inhibiting the P2Y12 receptor on platelets, which does not involve the inhibition of adenyl cyclase; therefore, option (b) is false. Clopidogrel has a lower incidence of myelotoxicity compared to ticlopidine, making option (c) true. Clopidogrel has a shorter duration of action than ticlopidine, which means option (d) is also false. Lastly, it is indeed recommended to interrupt clopidogrel treatment at least one week prior to surgical intervention, confirming option (e) as true.
